evidence.title: Local Law No. 3 of the Year 2026 -- A Local Law Imposing a Moratorium on the Establishment, Construction, Expansion, or Operation of Data Centers, Artificial Intelligence Processing Facilities, and Cryptocurrency Mining Operations Within the Town of Lewiston, Niagara County, New York
evidence.supports: Establishes that Local Law 3-2026 was enacted (it is filed under the Town's official '2026 Local Laws' directory with an assigned local-law number), sets an 18-month moratorium period, contains a SEQRA Type II Action determination, and shows the law's legislative findings are general and name no specific project or applicant.
evidence.quote: Effective upon the date of adoption of this Local Law, and continuing for a period of eighteen (18) months thereafter (the "Moratorium Period"), unless extended or earlier terminated by action of the Town Board, no person, entity, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, or other legal entity shall: (1) Establish, construct, build, install, place, operate, or use any Data Center, Artificial Intelligence Processing Facility, or Cryptocurrency Mining Operation within the Town of Lewiston...

decisions.notes: This document is the enacted law text itself, assigned an official local-law number and filed in the town's '2026 Local Laws' directory (which, per standard NY municipal practice, contains only adopted, filed local laws rather than proposals), which is strong evidence of adoption -- but the document does not itself display the Town Board's vote date or roll call, and I could not retrieve a readable version of the Town Board's own minutes (image-based/scanned PDF) or open blocked news coverage (wnypapers.com returned HTTP 403; niagara-gazette.com returned HTTP 429) to pin down the exact vote date or corroborate the 5-0 vote reported in search summaries. I am treating adoption and the 18-month term as established from the primary text, and the exact adoption date as approximately mid-to-late April 2026 (shortly after the 2026-04-13 public hearing) but unconfirmed to the day.
